title: Party leanings
legendIntro: Colour shows which of three party groups did best compared with its own share across Tokyo as a whole. It does not show who came first. For 1937 the three groups are only a rough fit for the parties of the time.
note: Three elections to the House of Representatives. Today: party-list (proportional) votes of 8 February 2026, by ward, city, town and village. Tokyo-wide shares: conservative 48.1%, centre 40.6%, left 9.9%. Sorting party lists into three groups is a judgement. Conservative: Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), Japan Innovation Party (Ishin), Sanseitō, Conservative Party of Japan; Centre: Centrist Reform Alliance, Democratic Party for the People, Team Mirai; Left: Japanese Communist Party, Reiwa Shinsengumi, Social Democratic Party. Not placed in any group: Tax Cuts Japan–Yūkoku Alliance (1.3% in Tokyo). 1960s: candidate votes of 29 January 1967, added up by party, for the ten districts Tokyo then had. Conservative: Liberal Democratic Party, plus independents the source calls conservative. Centre: Democratic Socialist Party and Kōmeitō. Left: Japan Socialist Party and Japanese Communist Party. Other independents and tiny parties are counted but left unplaced. Tokyo-wide shares: conservative 33.2%, centre 24.9%, left 37.0%. The 2nd district's totals include votes from the Izu islands, which are not drawn. District outlines are drawn from today's ward borders, so the four districts on the bay are approximate. 1930s: candidate votes of 30 April 1937, added up by party, for the seven districts Tokyo then had. Only men aged 25 and over could vote in 1937. Sorting the parties of 1937 into three groups is a rough fit. Conservative: Rikken Seiyūkai, plus the small nationalist parties Shōwakai, Kokumin Dōmei and Rikken Yōseikai. Centre: Rikken Minseitō. Left: Shakai Taishūtō and Nihon Musantō. Candidates with no party given, and the tiny Kinrō Nihontō, are counted but left unplaced. Tokyo-wide shares: conservative 30.8%, centre 35.2%, left 28.2%, unplaced 5.9%. The 5th district's totals include votes from the Izu islands, which are not drawn. District outlines are approximate: the city wards are drawn from 1930s ward shapes and the 7th from today's Tama borders. In every period an area is coloured dark when a group is 2.5 points or more above its Tokyo-wide share, light when it is 1 to 2.5 points above, and neutral otherwise.
